findings.claim: Every practice question across all 7 lessons is labelled on an AQA-style split: '15 marks - Extract Response', '25 marks - Essay Response', '4 marks - Quote Analysis', with mark ladders banded 1-15, 1-25 and 1-4.
findings.truth: Edexcel 1ET0 Section A (Shakespeare) is a two-part question worth 20 + 20. Part (a) is 20 marks, AO2 only, on a printed extract of about 30 lines. Part (b) is 20 marks, AO1 15 plus AO3 5, on the theme elsewhere in the play. No 4-mark question exists, and there is no SPaG or AO4 mark in this section.
findings.evidence: specs/edexcel/english-literature-1ET0.md lines 1102-1113 (two-part question, AO2 extract ~30 lines, AO1/AO3 part b, 80 marks, 1h45, closed book) and the raw-mark table at 1312-1350.

findings.claim: L2 exam tip: 'For the part (a) extract question (15 marks, AO2)'. L7 knowledge check 1 asks how many marks part (a) is worth and keys '15 marks'. L7 exam tip times the paper 15-20 minutes for part (a) and 25-30 for part (b).
findings.truth: Part (a) is 20 marks. The two parts are equal, so a student should give each about 25 minutes (Section A is 40 of 80 marks in 1h45). The knowledge check marked the true answer wrong.

findings.claim: Shylock is repeatedly quoted as calling the bond a 'merry jest' - in L2 content (x3, including a revision tip), L2 conclusion, L2 exam tip, an L2 knowledge-check option keyed correct, an L2 flashcard answer, the L4 exam tip, an L4 mark scheme, L7 content and the L7 conclusion.
findings.truth: The phrase is 'merry sport'. Shylock: 'Go with me to a notary, seal me there / Your single bond; and in a merry sport, / If you repay me not on such a day...' (1.3). 'Merry jest' appears nowhere in the play.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg #1515 line 755: 'Your single bond; and in a merry sport,'.

findings.claim: Shylock quoted as ‘Fair sir, you spat on me on Wednesday last’.
findings.truth: The line reads 'you spet on me on Wednesday last' (modernised in editions as 'spit'). 'Spat' is not the reading of any standard edition.

findings.claim: Four uses of the banned band name 'Level 5': L3 content ('argument that reaches Level 5'), L3 exam tip ('responses at Level 5'), L5 exam tip ('reaches Level 5'), L7 glossary 'perceptive' ('The Level 5 descriptor word').
findings.truth: The house validator rejects the whole unit on 'Level 1'..'Level 9'. Replaced with the house ladder wording 'the top band'.

findings.claim: L3 content: the ring 'belonged to Shylock's dead wife, Leah'; L3 key fact and flashcard: 'her dead mother's turquoise ring'; L6 content and flashcard the same.
findings.truth: The ring was Shylock's own, a gift from Leah before their marriage: 'It was my turquoise, I had it of Leah when I was a bachelor.' It is not Jessica's inheritance from her mother.

findings.claim: 'The Duke himself acknowledges this: if contracts are not honoured, Venice's trade will be destroyed.'
findings.truth: Antonio makes this argument, in 3.3, not the Duke: 'The Duke cannot deny the course of law, / For the commodity that strangers have / With us in Venice... Since that the trade and profit of the city / Consisteth of all nations.' The Duke never says it.

findings.claim: L6 Q1 sets an extract 'from “I am a tainted wether of the flock” to “Bid her be judge / Whether Bassanio had not once a love”' - about 275 lines apart. L7 Q5 sets one 'from “Three thousand ducats for three months” to “Antonio shall become bound”' - the two boundaries are in reverse order in the text.
findings.truth: Neither range is a printable extract. L6 Q1 retargeted on Antonio's farewell speech ('But little. I am armed and well prepared' to 'had not once a love', ~14 lines) with the mark scheme rewritten to match. L7 Q5 boundaries swapped to run from 'Three thousand ducats, well' to 'Three thousand ducats for three months, and Antonio bound'.

findings.claim: L5 content: 'Shylock exits the stage with four devastating words: “I am not well”. These are his last words in the play.' An L5 knowledge check asks 'What are Shylock's last words in the play?' and an L5 flashcard asks the same.
findings.truth: 'I am not well' sits in the middle of his exit speech. His last words are 'And I will sign it': 'I pray you give me leave to go from hence; / I am not well; send the deed after me / And I will sign it.'

findings.claim: Jessica quoted as saying '“I am ashamed to be my father’s child”, 2.3' in L6 content, and a knowledge-check stem quotes the same words.
findings.truth: The line is 'Alack, what heinous sin is it in me / To be ashamed to be my father's child!' She calls the shame a sin; the lesson's version reverses that framing and is not verbatim.

findings.claim: 'The play’s subtitle hints at this: it is called The Merchant of Venice'.
findings.truth: That is the title, not a subtitle.

findings.claim: L1 matching check asks students to 'Match each location to its role in the play' and includes 'The Ghetto'.
findings.truth: The play never mentions the ghetto - the lesson body says so itself. The item is sound as context, but the stem's 'in the play' is loose. Not worth an edit.
findings.evidence: L1 content: 'While Shakespeare does not explicitly mention the ghetto'.

findings.claim: L7 tells students 'Check your own exam board’s specimen paper for the exact mark split and timings' and 'divide your time... (check your specimen paper)'.
findings.truth: Not false, but this is a single-board unit; the hedge sends an Edexcel student away to look up a figure the unit now states (20 + 20). Worth Tom's eye on a rewrite pass, not a fact-check edit.

summary: No lesson is clean. Every practice question in all 7 lessons carried an AQA-style 15 + 25 + 4 mark split instead of Edexcel's 20 + 20 two-part question, one knowledge check keyed part (a) at 15 marks, four lessons contained the banned band name 'Level 5', and the fabricated quotation 'merry jest' (really 'merry sport') ran through three lessons including a keyed knowledge-check option. 116 edits, all FIX.
